stories.headline: Priyanka Gandhi meets flood victims, workers in Nilambur
stories.title: Priyanka Gandhi meets flood victims, workers in Nilambur
stories.summary: The MP meets relatives of a flood victim, rural and autorickshaw workers and assures them that she will take up their concerns with the authorities concerned
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, MP, met flood victims, rural workers, and autorickshaw workers during her visit to the Nilambur region on Wednesday (September 23, 2026).
She visited the house of Sajita, one of the six persons who died in the Kottapuzha flash flood at T.K. Colony, Amarambalam, on Sunday (September 20, 2026).
Ms. Vadra met Sajita’s relatives at Appankappu settlement at Pothukallu and enquired about their needs.
She assured the family that she would take up their concerns and extend support.
She later met workers under the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (VB-G RAM G) at Kurumbalangode, Chungathara.
The workers spoke about the difficulties they faced after the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme was replaced by the new scheme.
Ms. Vadra said the new scheme undermined the idea behind the employment guarantee law.
She assured the workers that she would raise their concerns with the Centre and press for measures to address them.
At Chungathara, she also met autorickshaw workers and heard their concerns.
The workers said rising fuel prices and the cost of spare parts were affecting their earnings.
They sought a fuel subsidy as an immediate measure.
They also demanded an increase in the pension paid through the Welfare Fund Board and loans from the fund for vehicle maintenance.

stories.headline: Opposition calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal after report on Election Commissioners’ dissent
stories.title: Opposition calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal after report on Election Commissioners’ dissent
stories.summary: Both ECs recorded formal objections regarding centralisation of poll roll database, “illegal” changes in Form 6, removal of voters in West Bengal, Goa; terming the CEC the “chief architect of vote chori”, Congress calls for SC-monitored probe
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Opposition parties on Wednesday (September 23, 2026) sought the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar after an Indian Express expose claimed that two of the three Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had formally recorded objections at least 14 times over the last 10 months.
The two ECs said major decisions were being made in the name of the full Election Commission of India without their knowledge, several of which they called “unauthorised and illegal”.

Declaring that “vote chori” is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on the Constitution, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that “the BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason.
Justice will be served.” He will hold a press conference on the matter on Thursday.

Opposition parties asked the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the report and Congress leader K.C. Venugopal demanded a Supreme Court-monitored impartial investigation to “expose the rot that has destroyed the ECI’s credibility”.
The CEC has no right to remain in office after the expose, he said.
The ECI responded on Wednesday (September 23, 2026), saying that all its actions have been in accordance with laws and instructions of the Commission.

Highlighting specific internal notes or observations spread over the 10-month period while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions, and initiatives gives only “one part of the picture”, it said.
According to the Indian Express report, both Election Commissioners red-flagged several key issues, led by the centralisation of the database of electoral rolls.
In May, Mr. Joshi had reportedly proposed an audit to certify that “no one except the concerned statutory authorities has any credentials to make any change in the data base”.

In August, Mr. Sandhu had recorded that State-level election officials were reporting that they do not have “proper and complete access” to the ERONet portal, the digital system through which the electoral rolls are maintained.

He further flagged that the Commission’s director general of information technology Seema Khanna “does not have any legal authority to restrict proper and complete access and freedom to operate as given by law to the statutory authorities”.

stories.headline: Mamata calls for Chief Election Commissioner’s arrest, seeks fresh West Bengal polls
stories.title: Mamata calls for Chief Election Commissioner’s arrest, seeks fresh West Bengal polls
stories.summary: Former Chief Minister says there will be a nationwide protest and that INDIA bloc leaders will meet soon, asserting that all Opposition parties are together in this ‘fight’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Raising allegations of vote theft in the Assembly elections in West Bengal and other States, former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday (September 23, 2026) called for the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar.

“Today, the entire country is in turmoil over Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and my first demand is that he should be arrested and criminal proceedings should be initiated against him,” Ms. Banerjee said, addressing a virtual press conference.
She also called for the “return” of elections that she claimed were “stolen”, saying that Opposition parties are united in the fight against the Election Commission (EC).
“Re-election must be held in West Bengal with the old voter list,” Ms. Banerjee said.

Her remarks came in the wake of a report by The Indian Express that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had purportedly red-flagged multiple issues during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in multiple States.
Ms. Banerjee said there would be a nationwide protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, and that leaders of the Opposition INDIA bloc would soon meet over the issue.
“All parties, including regional parties and INDIA alliance parties, are together in this battle....
This is no longer merely about impeachment; criminal action is required,” the leader of the Mamata.
All India Trinamool Congress said.
She also said that her party was the first to raise these issues seven to eight months before the election.
Ms. Banerjee demanded that action be taken not only against the Chief Election Commissioner, but also against those in the government and the EC who are responsible for the issues.
She claimed that her party’s symbol was taken away because she had protested against the EC’s actions.

stories.headline: 'Prime Minister's Nominee Can't Be Expected To Defy Him': Justice Datta Doubts Independence Of Election Commissioners' Selection Panel
stories.title: 'Prime Minister's Nominee Can't Be Expected To Defy Him': Justice Datta Doubts Independence Of Election Commissioners' Selection Panel
stories.summary: "If free and fair elections are to be ensured, it is axiomatic that the ECI must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently,” he observed.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: "If free and fair elections are to be ensured, it is axiomatic that the ECI must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently,” he observed.

Supreme Court justice Dipankar Datta today prima facie questioned the neutrality of the mechanism for appointing the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under the 2023 law, observing that the Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister cannot be expected to oppose the Prime Minister in the selection process.
Justice Datta prima facie observed that the Prime Minister-nominated Cabinet Minister could not be expected to act as an independent counterweight to the Prime Minister.

“The Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, to function as the third member on the Selection Committee chaired by the Prime Minister, cannot be expected to defy his own nominator and risk his continuation as such nominated member on the committee, for all practical purposes,” he observed.

Justice Dipankar Datta delivered his opinion on whether the challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 should be referred to a Constitutional Bench.

The petitions challenge Section 7 of the 2023 Act, which provides for a three-member Selection Committee comprising the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

Before deciding the issue of reference, he prima facie observed that free and fair elections require the Election Commission of India (ECI) to not only be independent but also to be seen to act independently.

The petitioners argued that the inclusion of the PM's nominee undermines the institutional neutrality of the Selection Committee, as the PM's nominee could not be expected to oppose him and support the Leader of Opposition.
Justice Datta found weight it the petitioners' argument and observed that with two members of the committee being from the executive, the executive effectively gets a veto over the selection process.

He highlighted, “When queried by this Court as to whether the Prime Minister's nominee would take a stand against the Prime Minister in case of a difference of opinion between the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition, 'probably no' was the answer of the learned Attorney although 'certainly no' is what the challengers say would be the ultimate outcome.”
Justice Datta observed that even the likelihood of a “no” to the Court's question was enough to affect the perception of the Selection Committee.
“The presence of likelihood of a 'no' is striking enough to colour the perception of the Selection Committee,” he observed.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court will hear Mamata Banerjee’s plea on September 24 challenging the Election Commission’s interim order freezing the Trinamool Congress party’s name and its reserved election symbol amid a dispute between rival factions.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court is slated to hear on Thursday Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee’s plea challenging the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) decision to freeze the party’s name and its reserved election symbol amid an ongoing dispute between rival factions.

The case is listed at serial number 26 before the CJI-led Bench as a fresh civil case for admission.

Mamata Banerjee has filed the plea against the ECI’s interim decision to freeze the name “All India Trinamool Congress” and its reserved “Flowers and Grass” election symbol amid the dispute between rival factions of the party.
The petition names the Election Commission of India, its Secretary and rebel leader Ritabrata Banerjee as respondents.
On Monday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Mamata Banerjee, had sought urgent listing of the plea before CJI Surya Kant.
“They (ECI) issue a by-poll notification and in the middle of the notification, they freeze the symbol.
We want urgent listing,” he submitted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Reserves Order On Noida DM Medha Roopam's Plea To Stay Allahabad HC Judgment Quashing Student's NSA Detention
stories.title: Supreme Court Reserves Order On Noida DM Medha Roopam's Plea To Stay Allahabad HC Judgment Quashing Student's NSA Detention
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(September 23) reserved order on the grant of interim relief in the petition filed by Gautam Buddh Nagar District(Noida) Magistrate Medha Roopam challenging the Allahabad High Court order, which directed compensation of Rs.5 lakhs to be paid from her salary for the detention of student Akriti Chaudhary under the National Security Act in connection with the Noida workers' protest.
The Court also heard a separate petition filed by the State of Uttar Pradesh challenging the High Court's order quashing the NSA detention of the student.
A bench comprising Justice Satish Chandra Sharma and Justice NK Singh after hearing the matter, reserved it for interim orders.
The bench had muted the audio of the VC proceedings during the hearing, blocking media access (reporters cannot physically enter the Supreme Court).
It is understood that the State and the officer argued against isolating the DM for fixing liability over the student's detention.
They pressed for staying the High Court's order and its strictures against the bureaucrat.
Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta, appearing for the District Magistrate, submitted that the strictures against the officer were "unwarranted".
He stated that there are several layers before the District Magistrate takes the decision.

Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for the State of UP, submitted that the Allahabad High Court's order is "totally uncalled for." He added that the respondent, Akriti Chaudhary, was "fomenting trouble" in Manesar in Haryana, and later the agitation shifted to Noida, which led to arson and destruction of public properties in April.
The proposal for detention was moved by the SHO, and ultimately passed by the DM.

The DM's order was approved by the advisory committee, and subsequently by the State Government and the Union Government under the National Security Act, he added, emphasising that the DM was only a "link in the chain." Rohatgi further contended that the High Court did not examine the NSA detention order, and its examination was only confined to whether the arrest was legal or not.
The audio of the proceedings was blocked at this juncture, denying further access to the proceedings.

The Court also heard a separate petition filed by the State of Uttar Pradesh challenging the High Court's order quashing the NSA detention of the student.
body: A bench comprising Justice Satish Chandra Sharma and Justice NK Singh after hearing the matter, reserved it for interim orders.
The bench had muted the audio of the VC proceedings during the hearing, blocking media access (reporters cannot physically enter the Supreme Court).
It is understood that the State and the officer argued against isolating the DM for fixing liability over the student's detention.
They pressed for staying the High Court's order and its strictures against the bureaucrat.
Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta, appearing for the District Magistrate, submitted that the strictures against the officer were "unwarranted".
He stated that there are several layers before the District Magistrate takes the decision.

Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for the State of UP, submitted that the Allahabad High Court's order is "totally uncalled for." He added that the respondent, Akriti Chaudhary, was "fomenting trouble" in Manesar in Haryana, and later the agitation shifted to Noida, which led to arson and destruction of public properties in April.
The proposal for detention was moved by the SHO, and ultimately passed by the DM.

stories.headline: Wipro Consumer Care Acquires Dermatouch
stories.title: Wipro Consumer Care Acquires Dermatouch
stories.summary: Wipro Consumer Care’s 18th acquisition, Dermatouch, marks its entry into India’s premium skincare segment and strengthens its global beauty and personal care portfolio
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Wipro Consumer Care & Lighting announced the acquisition of Dermatouch, one of India’s fastest-growing, science-backed premium skincare brands, marking its entry into India’s fast-growing premium skincare market.
This marks Wipro Consumer Care’s 18th acquisition globally and its third strategic acquisition this year.

This move reflects Wipro Consumer Care’s continued focus on building leadership in high-growth consumer categories by expanding into segments where consumers are increasingly seeking effective, dermatologist recommended solutions backed by science and efficacy.

Building on its global skincare expertise through brands such as Derma Lab, Dr. Dermis and Bio-essence, the acquisition represents Wipro Consumer Care’s strategic entry into India’s premium skincare segment.

Founded by Anish Nagpal and Amit Purswani, Dermatouch has emerged as one of India’s fast-growing, made-in-India, concern-based pharmacy skincare brands, focused on addressing a wide spectrum of evolving skin concerns and consumer needs.

Built around concerns such as pigmentation, acne, brightening and sun protection, the brand offers science-backed skincare solutions across formats ranging from face washes, soaps and serums to creams, moisturisers and sunscreens.

Dermatouch has built its proposition around efficacy, accessibility and a deep understanding of evolving skincare needs, with its products gaining strong consumer acceptance and being increasingly recommended by dermatologists.
The brand has built its presence through its direct-to-consumer platform, online marketplaces and an expanding offline retail network.
Their revenues in FY 26 were Rs.131 Cr (~US$ 13.6 Mn) with a growth of 114% over FY25.
Wipro will be acquiring a 60% stake at an Enterprise value of INR 387.5 Cr, with balance 40% to be acquired over the next 3 years.
Anish Nagpal, Amit Purswani and the current management team of Dermatouch will continue to run the business during this period.
Dermatouch has built its proposition around a fundamental shift in consumer behavior: skincare is increasingly moving from beauty-led choice to efficacy-led choice.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Frowns Upon PIL Challenging Inter-Se Assessment Of Tender Bids
stories.title: Supreme Court Frowns Upon PIL Challenging Inter-Se Assessment Of Tender Bids
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (September 23) has observed that a ₹23-crore road construction contract was not of such magnitude as to justify a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) on the ground of alleged wastage of public resources, particularly when the dispute essentially concerned the comparative eligibility of competing bidders.

A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu made the observation while hearing an appeal against a Himachal Pradesh High Court judgment that had quashed the award of a ₹23-crore Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (“PMGSY”) road project in favour of the Appellant-O.P. Mehta and directed re-tendering.
The Court questioned whether such a tender dispute could appropriately be brought through a PIL, noting that the challenge predominantly involved an inter-se comparison between two bidders.

“We have our reservations since the grounds raised in the PIL before the High Court of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla pre-dominantly dealt with, inter-se comparative assessment between the two bidders whose bids had been received…”, the Court said.
Importantly, the Court noted that the value of the work, approximately ₹23 crore, was not by itself sufficient to invoke public interest on the ground of wastage of public resources.
“Moreso even the cost of work (Rs.
23 crores) was not of such magnitude, which may allow the petitioner in PIL to raise the plea of wastage of public resources.”, the Court observed.
The Court also noted that the PIL petitioner was the “alter ego of the unsuccessful bidder”, who had complained against the successful bidder and subsequently withdrawn the complaint.

Taking note of the appellant's assurance to complete the remaining work within three months at the original rates and without compromising quality, the Court granted the appellant three months to complete the project.
If the work is not completed within that period, the authorities have been directed to re-tender the work at the prevailing market rate.
The matter will be listed in the first week of December 2026 for a compliance report.
For Petitioner(s):Mr. Anup Rattan, Advocate General Mr. Vaibhav Srivastava, A.A.G. Mr. Puneet Rajta, Adv.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Judges Urge CJI To Consider Constituting Permanent Constitution Bench, Flag Years-Long Delay In References
stories.title: Supreme Court Judges Urge CJI To Consider Constituting Permanent Constitution Bench, Flag Years-Long Delay In References
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday urged Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to consider constituting a permanent five-Judge Constitution Bench to decide pure constitutional questions, flagging the years-long delay in references to larger benches.
The Court observed that the inordinate delay in resolving references was a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders should strive to avoid.
“If statistics are any guide, none can say with any reasonable degree of certainty when long pending references will get resolved.

Undisputedly, this is an area of grave concern and the inordinate delay in resolution of the references is itself a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders ought to strive to avoid.
Self-introspection, indeed, is required,” it observed.

A bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma made the request while directing that the pleas challenging the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 be placed before the CJI for considering the constitution of a Constitution Bench.
The bench was divided on whether the challenge itself warranted a reference to a larger Bench.

Justice Datta held that the existing division bench could decide the challenge, while Justice Sharma held that the case involved a substantial question of constitutional interpretation requiring consideration by a Constitution Bench.
The judges, however, agreed that sending the issue of their difference of opinion to another three-judge bench would only delay the adjudication.
Thay addressed the concern raised by the petitioners regarding the time taken by the Supreme Court to decide references to Constitution Benches.
The Court noted that Anoop Baranwal.
Union of India originated from a writ petition under Article 32 filed in 2015.

stories.headline: Centre cuts customs duty on crude, refined sunflower, soybean and palm oils
stories.title: Centre cuts customs duty on crude, refined sunflower, soybean and palm oils
stories.summary: The duty reductions cover both crude and refined varieties, with the sharpest cut applying to crude sunflower oil imports
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'customs duty' in title weight 40
article_sentences: The Government on Wednesday cut basic customs duty on crude and refined varieties of sunflower, soybean and palm oil, a move which will help lower prices in the domestic market.
The basic customs duty (BCD) on crude.
Sunflower Oil has been reduced from 10 per cent to Nil, while the BCD on refined.
Sunflower Oil has been trimmed from 32.5 per cent to 22.5 per cent.
The BCD on crude Soybean Oil and Palm Oil has also been slashed from 10 per cent to 5 per cent and on refined Soybean Oil and Palm Oil from 32.5 per cent to 27.5 per cent.
The duty cuts will be effective from September 24, the finance ministry said in a notification.

stories.headline: DRDO scientist Gopinath K. takes charge as DMRL director
stories.title: DRDO scientist Gopinath K. takes charge as DMRL director
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'takes charge' in title weight 40
article_sentences: Eminent materials scientist and defence researcher Gopinath K. has assumed charge as director of the Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL), Hyderabad.
DMRL is a premier laboratory of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) dedicated to the development of advanced materials for India’s defence sector.

Prior to his appointment, Mr.Gopinath served as an Outstanding Scientist and Associate Director at DMRL, where he led several high-priority aeronautical materials projects and core research programmes.
He joined DRDO in 1994 and spent more than three decades contributing to the development of indigenous technologies critical to India’s national security.
Between 1994 and 2008, he played a key role in the indigenous development of materials and components for the Kaveri engine programme, working closely with multiple industries.

After moving to DMRL in 2008, he focused on advancing high-temperature materials and specialised naval steels, contributing significantly to the development of critical technologies for India’s naval and aerospace platforms.
An alumnus of some of the country’s leading engineering and research institutions, Mr.Gopinath earned his B.E. from PSG College of Technology, Coimbatore in 1992, M.Tech.
from IIT Kanpur in 1994 and Ph.D. from IISc-Bengaluru in 2009, said a press release on Wednesday.
